observations: Kraken last is 0.83% below its rolling 24h VWAP and 2.13% below its UTC-day open. OKX last is 2.26% below its rolling 24h open. These are descriptive venue-specific comparisons.
Both direct spot observations are near their respective reported 24h lows, but timestamps and quote currencies differ.

TradRadar reports declining OI, positive OI-weighted funding, an 80% long-account share and long-dominated liquidations. This is consistent with long-side deleveraging while residual long positioning remains.

Alpha Finance reports materially higher aggregate OI and modelled liquidation clusters. Its OI scope is not reconciled to TradRadar; its liquidation clusters are estimates rather than observed resting orders.
ETF dashboards show approximately 1.20B XRP held but differ in AUM, product counts, fund universe and flow cutoff. Their holdings-derived totals are not direct cash creations/redemptions.
competing_hypotheses: Long-liquidation dominance and declining OI may represent forced long deleveraging; if forced selling exhausts, the flow may stabilize without implying a reversal.
Positive weighted funding and a high long-account share may indicate residual long positioning, leaving the market vulnerable to further downside if nearby support fails.
The $860M OI difference may be caused by provider contract coverage, aggregation methods, notional conversion or timestamp differences; neither aggregate is accepted as the universal total.
ETF dashboard differences may reflect different fund universes, update timing, holdings valuation and incomplete issuer files rather than contradictory primary flows.
disconfirming_or_missing_evidence: Kraken ticker response has no provider timestamp; exact server time cannot be established from the response.
OKX provider timestamp is 26 minutes old at retrieval and fails the 300-second live-feature freshness gate.
No synchronized multi-level order book or market-impact ladder was captured; only Level-1 quote sizes are available.
Direct Binance spot depth, Binance perpetual OI/mark, OKX perpetual OI/funding, and OKX multi-level books were not retrievable through this web path.
